limitations: Illustrative capital only — not HK RBC compliant
Assets only: no insurance liabilities, hedges, tax, operational risk, concentration or FX risk.

Counterfactual model attribution is not a transaction ledger, investment return, or proof of economic causality.
Date ageing is applied first at opening bond quotes; its interactions with market/holding changes are allocated by that explicit ordering.
Equity/cash market-value changes jointly represent quantities, prices and flows; units and trade data are unavailable, so these causes cannot be separated.

A flat scalar risk-free yield and scalar credit spread are independent input factors; no observed yield-curve, liquidity/default decomposition or official HK RBC calibration is implied.

source_references.title: Insurance (Valuation and Capital) Rules, L.N. 62 of 2024 — Capital adequacy thresholds
source_references.text: Subject to rule 5(2), an applicable insurer must maintain capital base at least equal to each of its prescribed capital amount, minimum capital amount and HK$20 million. Capital base follows Part 3; PCA follows Part 5.
source_references.provenance: Official-domain text surfaced by web search index; full PDF retrieval unavailable in this session.

source_references.limitations: Historical baseline only; requires insurer applicability, valuation date, variations/relaxations and current official text. Does not establish a complete regulatory calculation.

source_references.text: MCA is 50% of PCA unless the IA determines another amount through the variation or relaxation mechanism in rule 5(2).
